topics.topic: Aggregate byte and file-count limits for scratch storage
questions: May one execution create arbitrarily many individually conforming scratch files, or is the exchange directory also subject to an aggregate byte or file-count limit?

What happens when code creates many individually conforming scratch files and exhausts aggregate bytes, inodes or host storage, since the changed rule no longer bounds the exchange directory as a whole?
Is there any bound on the aggregate bytes or number of scratch files, and how is exhaustion of the backing filesystem classified when every individual file remains within the per-file bound?

quotes: The scratch bound is the host kernel's file-size limit on every file the code writes (the runner ignores SIGXFSZ, so the write fails with EFBIG); the exchange directory as a whole has no separate bound in this release.
Only EFBIG is a scratch hit; exhausted host storage (ENOSPC, EDQUOT) is an ordinary error, and code killed by SIGXFSZ after restoring its default exited abnormally — both `crashed` (round 116).
judgement.why: State 8 specifies a per-file limit with no aggregate directory limit and classifies host-storage exhaustion.

topics.topic: Exact process-count limit and which runner, processes, or identities it counts
questions: Does `process_count` include the already-running sandbox runner, and what exact RLIMIT_NPROC value must be installed?
What exact process limit is set, and does `process_count` include the already-running in-sandbox runner?
Does `process_count` include the in-sandbox runner, and which processes or user identity are counted by the process limit?

quotes: The runner MUST set every setrlimit limit inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code, soft and hard alike (every limit is set soft and hard to the same value; bubblewrap is started without any capability option, so the code holds none and cannot raise a limit): address space at bounds.memory_bytes, the size of a file written in the scratch at the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, and the outer process bound, the limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1;

process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks.
judgement.why: State 8 fixes RLIMIT_NPROC at process_count plus one and defines exactly which tasks process_count counts.

topics.topic: Meaning of sandbox-owned enforcement and the normative effect of decision 30
questions: What subject is governed by “how is the sandbox's own”: the choice of enforcement mechanism, the implementation of all limits, or some other behavior, and which observable requirements does decision 30 impose?
What is “how” referring to, and which enforcement responsibility is assigned to the sandbox rather than the parent?
What does “how” refer to, and does the unavailable `decision 30` impose normative requirements beyond the limits and outcomes written here?

quotes: The runner sets address space, the file size in the scratch and `RLIMIT_NPROC` inside the sandbox's user namespace, before the code is loaded, soft and hard alike; the code holds no capability, so it cannot raise one.
The parent keeps, from outside, the wall deadline and the output count.
judgement.why: Decision 30 explicitly assigns setrlimit enforcement to the in-sandbox runner and deadline and output-count enforcement to the parent.

topics.topic: Processes and lifecycle phases covered by memory and process resource bounds
questions: Exactly which sandbox and runner processes and which phases of their lifetime are charged to `memory_bytes`, `process_count` and the scratch-file limit?

Which processes and phases must the contract's memory and process bounds cover: only the code-running interpreter, the runner and all descendants, or also bubblewrap and sandbox setup before the limits are installed?

Must the address-space limit be installed before the Python interpreter and runner are loaded, or only before the agent module is loaded, and do the runtime, inputs and runner count against `memory_bytes`?

quotes: The runner MUST set every setrlimit limit inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code, soft and hard alike (every limit is set soft and hard to the same value; bubblewrap is started without any capability option, so the code holds none and cannot raise a limit): address space at bounds.memory_bytes, the size of a file written in the scratch at the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, and the outer process bound, the limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1;

process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks.
judgement.why: State 8 places the limits in the already-running runner before agent code loads and expressly excludes bubblewrap processes from process_count.

topics.topic: Resource bounds and scratch limits used by the startup probe
questions: Which limits and values must the start probe install, and must startup fail if any release-ceiling limit cannot be installed?
What ResourceBounds and scratch-file limit must the startup probe use, now that the rule saying it uses the current release ceilings has been removed?
What resource bounds and scratch-file behavior must the start probe use, especially after a release lowers ceilings or when stored older contracts have larger bounds?

quotes: probe_sandbox's probe execution runs the same runner with the current release ceilings, so a host that refuses them does not start, while an earlier contract version's larger bounds (A20 rule 4) are set only when it executes and are crashed where the host refuses them;

probe_sandbox: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise SandboxUnavailableError naming what is missing when the bubblewrap executable, bwrap, cannot be found on the process's PATH, when bwrap --version, which prints "bubblewrap" and the version, names a version other than the imported RELEASE_BWRAP_VERSION constant, when the resolved interpreter path os.path.realpath(sys.executable) lies under no path of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant, when that interpreter, the one execute_function starts inside bubblewrap, run once through bwrap with the same read-only bindings of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant and the same links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant to print platform.python_implementation() and platform.python_version() joined by one space, does not print exactly the imported RELEASE_SANDBOX_INTERPRETER constant, or when one probe execution through execute_function of a minimal implementation with no ports, under bounds equal to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_WALL_TIME_MS, RELEASE_CEILING_MEMORY_BYTES, RELEASE_CEILING_OUTPUT_BYTES and RELEASE_CEILING_PROCESS_COUNT constants, does not end succeeded, naming its outcome.
judgement.why: State 8 requires the probe to use the same runner with all current release-ceiling bounds and makes any non-success stop startup.

topics.topic: Whether a caught resource-limit rejection still irreversibly counts as resource exhaustion and how it is recorded
questions: Must any attempted operation rejected by one of these limits irreversibly classify the execution as `resource_exhausted`, even if the implementation catches the resulting exception, and how is that hit observed?

Does an attempted operation that the OS refuses because of a resource limit count as a limit hit even when agent code catches the resulting exception or signal and returns conforming output, and how must the sandbox preserve that fact?

quotes: The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the runner's limit on the number of processes, process_count + 1, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).

A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside — the parent kills an environment for its wall deadline alone, and a process killed by a signal, SIGXFSZ included, exited abnormally: a MemoryError or an OSError with errno EFBIG for a file past the file-size limit escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned, like any other output (owner, 2026-10-06).
Only the process bound is also seen inside, because every thread start and os.fork passes the runner's audit hook.
judgement.why: State 8 distinguishes process-limit rejections, which remain resource_exhausted when caught, from caught memory or scratch errors, which are judged by the returned output.

questions: Which scratch write failures are `resource_exhausted`, and which are `crashed` or ordinary exceptions visible to the implementation?
